body.statement: Given \(S\), \(u\), and the quotient rank oracle, a strongly polynomial submodular-function-minimization algorithm returns \(\kappa_0(S)\), \(\eta(S)\), \(r_{\mathrm{gen}}(S)\), and a maximizing deficient set \(I^*\subseteq\mathcal D_S\) using a number of oracle calls polynomial in \(|\mathcal D_S|\). Each oracle call is an exact rank computation over \(\mathbb F_S\); hence the output is an exact certificate rather than a numerical generic-rank guess.
body.justification: The theorem turns exponentially many Hall inequalities into an executable exact certificate with a named obstruction.
body.gap: Schrijver supplies oracle submodular minimization and Hirai and Iwamasa handle a narrow independently parameterized block-matrix class; neither constructs the fortified quotient rank oracle.
body.consumer: Sensitivity analyses over defended proxy subsets can report the precise support blocks responsible for route failure instead of only a failed matrix-rank check.
body.proof_tex:
For \(I\subseteq\mathcal D_S\), define
\[
\rho(I)=\mathcal O_S(I)
=\dim_{\mathbb F_S}\left(\sum_{(y,j)\in I}W_y\right),
\qquad F(I)=\rho(I)-|I|.
\]
The function \(\rho\) is submodular.  Indeed, with \(U_I=\sum_{e\in I}W_e\), the dimension identity and the inclusion \(U_{I\cap J}\subseteq U_I\cap U_J\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho(I)+\rho(J)
&=\dim(U_I+U_J)+\dim(U_I\cap U_J)\\
&\ge \dim U_{I\cup J}+\dim U_{I\cap J}
=\rho(I\cup J)+\rho(I\cap J).
\end{aligned}
\]
The modular function \(I\mapsto |I|\) satisfies equality in the same relation, so \(F=\rho-|\cdot|\) is submodular and integer-valued.  Apply the cited strongly polynomial submodular-minimization theorem to \(F\).  If \(I^*\) is the returned minimizer, then
\[
\eta(S)=\max_I\{|I|-\rho(I)\}=-\min_I F(I)=-F(I^*),
\]
so \(I^*\) is an exact maximizing deficient set.

It remains to compute the constant-direction defect.  From the matrices specified in the rank-oracle definition, exact Gaussian elimination over \(\mathbb F_S\) gives bases for \(H_S=\ker D_S\), \(R_S(x)\), \(L_S(x)=H_S+R_S(x)\), its annihilator \(N_S(x)\), and \(J_S\).  A second elimination yields
\[
\kappa_0(S)=\dim(N_S(x)\cap J_S)
=\dim N_S(x)+\dim J_S-\dim(N_S(x)+J_S).
\]
Finally the generic-rank formula returns
\[
r_{\mathrm{gen}}(S)=Q_S-\kappa_0(S)-\eta(S).
\]
Schrijver's algorithm makes polynomially many calls in \(|\mathcal D_S|\); all other displayed computations use polynomially many field operations on the finite input matrices.  By the definition of \(\mathcal O_S\), every oracle value and every auxiliary dimension is obtained by exact rational-function elimination.  Thus no floating-point specialization or probabilistic rank test enters the certificate.  The strong-polynomial assertion here is the stated oracle-call assertion; it does not assert a strongly polynomial bit-complexity bound for representing arbitrary rational functions.
